dataset.name: Aerial Data and Processed Models of Port Arthur Coastal Neighborhood and Pleasure Island Golf Course, June 2024
description: Our Co-design team is from the University of Texas, working on a Department of Energy-funded project focused on the Beaumont-Port Arthur area. As part of this project, we will be developing climate-resilient design solutions for areas of the region. More on www.caee.utexas.edu.
We captured aerial photos in the Port Arthur Coastal Neighborhood Community and the Golf Course on Pleasure Island, Texas, in June 2024.

Aerial photos taken were through DroneDeploy autonomous flight, and models were processed through the DroneDeploy engine as well. All aerial photos are in .JPG format and contained in zipped files for each area.

The processed data package includes 3D models, geospatial data, mappings, and point clouds. Please be aware that DTM, Elevation toolbox, Point cloud, and Orthomosaic use EPSG: 6588. And 3D Model uses EPSG: 3857.
- The Adobe Suite gives you great software to open .Tif files.
- You can use LASUtility (Windows), ESRI ArcGIS Pro (Windows), or Blaze3D (Windows, Linux) to open a LAS file and view the data it contains.
- Open an .OBJ file with a large number of free and commercial applications. Some examples include Microsoft 3D Builder, Apple Preview, Blender, and Autodesk.
- You may use ArcGIS, Merkaartor, Blender (with the Google Earth Importer plug-in), Global Mapper, and Marble to open .KML files.
- The .tfw world file is a text file used to georeference the GeoTIFF raster images, like the orthomosaic and the DSM. You need suitable software like ArcView to open a .TFW file.

This dataset provides researchers with sufficient geometric data and the status quo of the land surface at the locations mentioned above. This dataset could streamline researchers' decision-making processes and enhance the design as well.

measurementTechnique:
PLAN THE DRONE FLIGHT
I decided to use DroneDeploy for this mission, so I used DroneDeploy to plan the flights as well.
**Drone Flight Instruction (Incl. contacts, cautions, tips).pdf is under SETx_UIFL > Theme 2 Co-Design > Visualization under Deep Uncertainty.
Certain flights may require permissions from LAANC (Low Altitude Authorization and Notification Capability); To acquire permissions 72 hours prior to departure because LAANC will not send any permission within 72 hours.
To get well-prepared flight paths because flight height can affect resolution and to improve the quality of 3D structures with a perimeter or crosshatch flight path.

FLIGHT PERMISSIONS
Permissions were obtained from local authorities for each flight.

DURING THE DRONE FLIGHT
Frequently check Battery level and SD card storage when fly autonomously.
Set up timed(2s) shooting for getting a more stable drone camera gimbal to get higher quality photos.
Frequently perform data QA/AC for each location.
Store data to the DroneDeploy or any backup storage for each location.

AFTER THE DRONE FLIGHT
Check the quality of the photos, then delete mistaken and low-resolution photos.
Upload aerial photos to SETx_UIFL > Theme 2 Co-Design.
Upload aerial photos to DroneDeploy to generate point cloud and 3D model.
Check accuracy of the map and 3D model
Check Orthomosaic Resolution and any issue.
